assumptions.description: The set $K\subset\mathbb R^d$ is hidden, nonempty, compact, and convex. An enclosing ball, diameter bound $D_K$, and feasible point $z_0$ are public. The operator $F$ is monotone and $\beta$-Lipschitz on $K$.
assumptions.scope: The complete stated domain. Constants remain uniform when the other variable block is fixed.

description_paragraphs: The set $K\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ is hidden, nonempty, compact, and convex. An enclosing ball, a diameter bound $D_K$, and a feasible point $z_0$ are public. The operator $F$ is monotone and $\beta$-Lipschitz on $K$.
The complete analytic set description is hidden. No extra information sufficient for free projection is supplied.
source_fields.instance: Solve the monotone VI $0\in F(z)+N_K(z)$, measuring error by weak gap.
source_fields.parameter_domain_description: $D_K$: positive real; $\beta$: positive real; $d$: positive integer; $\varepsilon$: positive real. Derived quantities are defined in the parameter table; additional accuracy and dimension conditions appear in each regime.

source_fields.finiteness_conditions: Use the compact-domain, solution-existence, and smoothness assumptions in the model and the stated metric definition.
source_fields.normalization: The exact formula governs; norms, squares, maxima, and expectations are not interchanged.

source_fields.cost: vector (N_operator_value,N_LMO); no default sum or free projection
source_fields.coupling: fixed legal tie-breaking oracle; quantifier is over all legal tie choices
description_paragraphs:
$$
z\in K\longmapsto F(z),\qquad c\in\mathbb{R}^d\longmapsto s(c)\in\arg\min_{s\in K}\langle c,s\rangle.
$$
Both responses are exact. Ties in linear minimization are resolved by an admissible deterministic rule fixed before interaction. Correctness is required for every such rule.
source_fields.operation_1: at feasible z, return F(z) exactly
source_fields.operation_2: for arbitrary c in R^d, return a feasible atom s(c) in argmin_{s in K}<c,s>

operations.coupling: The exact response map is fixed before interaction; repeated calls are charged separately.

description_paragraphs: The joint budget is $(N_F,N_{\rm LMO})$; each operation adds $1$ to its corresponding coordinate. Preserve jointly attainable budgets. Without specified weights, do not sum coordinates or combine coordinatewise bounds from different algorithms.
A fixed joint budget $(B_F,B_{\rm LMO})$ requires $N_F\le B_F$ and $N_{\rm LMO}\le B_{\rm LMO}$ on every admissible instance and every execution path. Early stopping within this budget is allowed.

Count all information calls for one instance and one requested accuracy, including initialization. Exact-real arithmetic, storage, and solving known models from public inputs and returned data are uncharged. This query-complexity quantity does not certify arithmetic or bit complexity.
source_fields.precision_model: Exact real information; internal arithmetic, storage, and bit costs are excluded from the query count.
source_fields.scalarization: Keep joint budgets when cost weights are unspecified. Project only onto an explicitly designated primary query coordinate.
source_fields.setup_cost: All charged initialization queries are included in the total budget.
